evals.query: Scaffold a contract-first Kora 2.x HTTP server in Java from an OpenAPI spec with GET /pets/{petId}. Wire the Gradle generation and implement the delegate so it returns the pet or 404.
expected_behavior: Puts io.koraframework:openapi-generator:$koraVersion on the buildscript classpath and applies the org.openapi.generator Gradle plugin, treating the two versions as separate things
Uses koraVersion=2.0.0.RC1 from plain mavenCentral() and the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform, never ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent
Registers a GenerateTask with generatorName = "kora", configOptions mode = "java-server", and a unique outputDir wired into sourceSets.main and compileJava.dependsOn
Adds annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" and implementation "io.koraframework:http-server-undertow" plus json-common
Implements PetApiDelegate as an @Component (io.koraframework.common.annotation.Component) returning PetApiResponses.GetPetByIdApiResponse.GetPetById200ApiResponse or ...GetPetById404ApiResponse
Plugs UndertowPublicHttpServerModule and JsonModule into @KoraApp
Does not return ResponseEntity, does not hand-write @HttpController/@HttpRoute for the generated API, and does not edit build/generated

evals.query: Same contract, but generate a Kotlin Kora 2.x server and implement the delegate.
expected_behavior: Sets configOptions mode = "kotlin-server"; does not offer kotlin-suspend-server or kotlin-reactive-server
Adds the KSP plugin and ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") together with the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform
Makes BOTH the ksp tasks and compileKotlin depend on the generate task, and adds the outputDir to kotlin.sourceSets.main
Implements the delegate as a plain (non-suspend) fun returning the sealed PetApiResponses type, annotated with @Component
Does not use ksp("ru.tinkoff.kora:symbol-processors") and does not mark any delegate function suspend

evals.query: Our Kora 1.x build used configOptions mode = "java-reactive-server" and the Kotlin service used "kotlin-suspend-server". Port both to Kora 2.0.
expected_behavior: States that only java-client, java-server, kotlin-client and kotlin-server remain in Kora 2.0
Maps java-reactive-server and java-async-server to java-server, kotlin-suspend-server to kotlin-server, and the corresponding client modes to java-client / kotlin-client
Explains that generation fails outright with "Invalid OpenAPI generator `mode`" listing the supported values
Rewrites the delegate implementations as synchronous methods returning the sealed *ApiResponses type directly
Removes Mono/Flux/CompletionStage return types, the reactor-core dependency added for the reactive mode, and any suspend modifier
Does not suggest keeping a reactive mode, does not reintroduce Context, and does not claim a compatibility flag exists

evals.query: The contract has status: type string with enum [available, pending, sold]. In the delegate I wrote Pet.StatusEnum.valueOf(status) and it throws for "available". Fix it, in Java and Kotlin.
expected_behavior: Uses Pet.StatusEnum.fromValue(status), the static factory the Kora generator emits on every enum
Explains that the generated constant is AVAILABLE while the wire value is "available", so Enum.valueOf compares against the wrong string and fails only on real data, never at compile time
Catches IllegalArgumentException and returns the contract's declared 400 response record
Rejects a hand-written statusOf helper, a values() scan by name(), and valueOf(raw.toUpperCase())
Mentions getValue() for serialising back to the wire value
Does not edit the generated enum and does not add a Jackson annotation to work around it

evals.query: After migrating to Kora 2.0 every request to a secured route returns 401. My extractor is annotated @Tag(ApiSecurity.SecurityRequirementTag1.class) and the contract declares a BearerAuth securityScheme.
expected_behavior: Identifies the ordinal SecurityRequirementTagN name as Kora 1.x — it does not exist in 2.0, so the extractor is never matched and the generated interceptor always answers 401
Changes the tag to the marker named after the security scheme: @Tag(ApiSecurity.BearerAuth.class) / @Tag(ApiSecurity.BearerAuth::class)
Explains the naming rule: the key under components.securitySchemes, PascalCased (oAuth2ClientCredentials becomes ApiSecurity.OAuth2ClientCredentials)
Imports ApiSecurity from the configured apiPackage, not from a Kora framework package
Supplies HttpServerPrincipalExtractor<String, Principal> whose extract returns null for an unauthenticated request, using PrincipalWithScopes only for oauth2 schemes
Does not add ApiSecurity to the @KoraApp extends list — it is a @Module and is discovered automatically
Does not return CompletableFuture from the extractor and does not introduce a non-Kora security framework

evals.query: In my Kotlin Kora 2.0 delegate I construct the generated model positionally: Pet(1L, "Fido", "dog"). After a contract change the values ended up in the wrong fields. What is the rule?
expected_behavior: States that generated Kotlin models keep the spec property order with optional properties (carrying defaults) interleaved among required ones, so positional arguments are not stable
Requires named arguments for both construction and copy(): Pet(id = 1L, name = "Fido", tag = "dog") and pet.copy(name = newName)
Explains that a positional call can still compile when the shifted types happen to line up, so the failure is silent
Mentions the Java counterpart: the generated required-only constructor and the withX(...) copy methods
Does not suggest editing the generated model, reordering the schema, or adding an @JvmOverloads-style workaround

evals.query: I want to add a response header and some logging to GET /pets, so I wrote my own @HttpController with @HttpRoute(method = "GET", path = "/pets") next to the generated one. Requests behave inconsistently.
expected_behavior: Explains that two handlers are now registered for the same method and path, so which one wins is non-deterministic
Directs the work to the generated *ApiDelegate as the only implementation point, and never to build/generated
For the header: declares it under that response in the contract so it becomes a component of the generated response record
For logging/cross-cutting behaviour: an HttpServerInterceptor wired through configOptions.extensions (interceptorType/interceptorTag), or globally with @Tag(HttpServer.class)
Mentions that the 1.x global tag @Tag(HttpServerModule.class) still compiles but is never looked up, so the interceptor silently never runs
Mentions the supported escape hatch of replacing a generated @DefaultComponent HttpServerResponseMapper with your own @Component one
Does not suggest keeping the duplicate controller or removing the generated one

evals.query: Gradle configuration fails with: Dependency requires at least JVM runtime version 25. This build uses a Java 21 JVM. My build already sets toolchain languageVersion 25.
expected_behavior: Explains that io.koraframework:openapi-generator is on the buildscript classpath, which is resolved by the JVM running Gradle, not by the project toolchain
States that a Java 25 toolchain block cannot fix it
Fixes the Gradle JVM itself: JAVA_HOME, org.gradle.java.home in gradle.properties, or the IDE's Gradle JVM setting
Notes that Kora 2.0 artifacts are compiled to class-file 69 (Java 25), so 25+ is a hard floor
Does not suggest downgrading Kora, removing the buildscript dependency, or adding --add-opens/--enable-preview as a workaround

evals.query: I renamed apiPackage and modelPackage. Now the build fails with "package ru.tinkoff.kora.example.api does not exist" and the errors point at files under build/generated. Should I just fix those files?
expected_behavior: Says no — never edit anything under build/generated; the next generation run overwrites it and the error returns

Explains the cause: the generator writes output but never deletes files from a previous run, and the Gradle build-cache key ignores apiPackage/modelPackage, so old and new package trees coexist in one source set
Prescribes ./gradlew clean build --no-build-cache on the first build after such a rename
Recommends one outputDir per spec so tasks cannot overwrite each other
Does not suggest excluding files from the source set, deleting individual generated files by hand, or adding them to .gitignore as a fix

evals.query: Add server-side validation to a Kora 2.x OpenAPI POST /pets endpoint: name 1-64 chars, weight between 0 and 500. Return HTTP 400 with our own error body.
expected_behavior: Sets configOptions enableServerValidation = "true" and notes it is read only in a server mode
Adds implementation "io.koraframework:validation-module" and ValidationModule (io.koraframework.validation.module.ValidationModule) to @KoraApp
Explains the generated annotations come from io.koraframework.validation.common.annotation (@Size, @Range, @Valid, @Validate) and that the controller, not the delegate, carries them
Supplies a ViolationExceptionHttpServerResponseMapper as a @KoraApp default method, keeping enableServerValidationInterceptor at its default true
Warns that only one constraint annotation is generated per property, so a string with both maxLength and pattern gets @Size only
Does not use Jakarta Bean Validation or Hibernate Validator, and does not add annotations to generated files

evals.query: My OpenAPI schema uses a discriminator with oneOf/allOf. What does the Kora 2.x generator produce and how do I handle it in the delegate?
expected_behavior: Describes the output: a @Json @JsonDiscriminatorField("<propertyName>") sealed interface, with each mapped variant a record/data class carrying @JsonDiscriminatorValue({...})
Requires the discriminator property to exist on the base schema and be listed in required
Handles the value with an exhaustive switch pattern match (Java) or when (Kotlin) over the sealed type, without a default branch
Notes that several mapping keys may resolve to one variant, which then carries multiple @JsonDiscriminatorValue entries
Treats openapiNormalizer DISABLE_ALL as an escape hatch for a mangled spec, not as a required default
Does not rely on reflection-based polymorphism, Jackson subtype annotations, or invented generator options

evals.query: Our migrated build still passes configOptions interceptors, additionalContractAnnotations and enableJsonNullable, plus delegateMethodBodyMode: "throw-exception". Nothing seems to happen. Fix the task.
expected_behavior: Explains that the Kora generator reads a fixed set of configOptions keys and silently ignores anything else, so a stale key produces no error and no effect
Replaces interceptors with configOptions.extensions, using interceptorType and/or interceptorTag under "*", "tags" or "operations"
Replaces additionalContractAnnotations with extensions.*.additionalMethodAnnotations
Drops enableJsonNullable: JsonNullable<T> is applied automatically to fields that are nullable and not required
Corrects delegateMethodBodyMode to "throwException", and warns that the generated *ApiModule default delegate is not @DefaultComponent, so it collides with a hand-written @Component delegate
Does not invent option names and does not claim Mustache templateDir overrides still customise output

evals.query: I need two OpenAPI contracts generated into one Kora 2.x application, both with security schemes. How do I configure that without conflicts?
expected_behavior: Registers a separate GenerateTask per contract, each with a unique outputDir
Gives each task its own apiPackage and modelPackage and wires both output directories into the source set
Adds compileJava.dependsOn (Java) or both ksp and compileKotlin dependsOn (Kotlin) for each task
Notes each spec produces its own ApiSecurity, so principal-extractor tags must be qualified by the right apiPackage
Implements one @Component delegate per generated *ApiDelegate
Does not reuse a single outputDir and does not edit files under build/generated
